title: Newt kidney tubules keep correct lumen size when cell size changes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Newt kidney tubules keep correct lumen size when cell size changes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Newt kidney tubules normally made of 8 to 10 cells in cross-section are built from fewer cells when cell size is experimentally enlarged, and from a single cell wrapping around itself when cells are made very large, showing that different molecular mechanisms (cell-cell interactions vs cytoskeletal deformation) can be deployed to reach the same anatomical outcome.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Multi-Scale Competency of Growth and Form

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Even more remarkable than the scaling of the cell number to unexpected size changes (on an ontogenetic, not evolutionary, timescale) is the fact that if the cells are made really huge, just one cell wraps around itself and still makes a proper lumen (Figure 6D).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Multi-Scale Competency of Growth and Form”. Scope: Polyploid newt larvae (Fankhauser's experiments)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The anatomical measurements are clear and historical images can test the qualitative result. Lack of raw specimens and quantitative records limits precision and causal analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure cell size, number of cells around each tubule, lumen diameter, and single-cell wrapping in normal and polyploid newt histology, testing whether lumen dimensions remain stable as construction mode changes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mechanistic deployment is inferred from geometry.

Evidence is historical and may consist mainly of published micrographs.

Original specimen-level measurements are unlikely to be deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.72
data existence: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.3
analysis feasibility: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Cell number, cell size, and lumen size are the variables Fankhauser published for newt tubules, including the single-cell case. Those counts can be compiled from the papers and cannot be remeasured from a public image set. The further claim that distinct molecular mechanisms are deployed for the same lumen is an interpretation of the geometry rather than a result in the old plates.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In polyploid newt larvae, count cells per tubule cross-section, cell size, and lumen diameter; the anatomical claim holds if larger cells yield fewer cells per cross-section and the largest cells form a one-cell lumen of normal size.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The measurements are in 1945 plates and counts, not a digital archive.

Cytoskeletal bending versus cell-cell signaling was inferred from the geometry, not measured with molecular markers.

The sample is one amphibian under classical polyploidy methods.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.55
